main_body: Grey steel safe body with a recessed door panel holding a gold dial/handle, seen mostly face-on
top_band: light grey L=170 rows 10-12 (3 rows), front-edge highlight L=215 at row 13, then darker L=126 at rows 14-15, which acts as an eave shadow
evidence: The column at x=4 shows a 3-row grey top (rows 10-12), a bright edge line at row 13 and a 2-row shadow at rows 14-15. The front face below (rows 17-25) is the same L=170 as the top. The top is thin, only about 3 of 22 rows, and the drawing is dominated by a face-on door with a dial. This reads as a front elevation with a thin hat, not a 3/4 box, and it is a doubtful case, so it fails under the strict rule. The inset door frame and the edge line are the only construction cues, and they do not make up for the short, foreshortened-looking top.

style.evidence: All dark edge pixels are neutral (100% near-neutral, #22282e), which is the sticker-style black outline, whereas the references are 1% and 33%. The candidate has only 10 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and its median per tile is 10 against 17-20. The grey ramp has about 4 steps (#22282e, #4a5460, #76808a, #a3acb5, #d0d8e0) plus a small gold accent. The surfaces are clean but have no grain, speckle or per-material texture, so it looks thinner and flatter than the Beodeul references. The 0% flat-fill figure only reflects the small size of the piece.
